comparator.name: International Business Administration
comparator.institution: Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University Rotterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The visually inspected2026–2027 TER Annex1 page20 is the controlling current framework, with60EC in each year. Its curriculum chart is a raster image and is absent from extracted text; Annex2 old-degree tables must not supply its credits. The selected30EC choice pathway is a15EC approved minor plus three5EC electives; Annex4 page29 places the last elective in block3.3 alongside Advanced Research Skills. Articles3.5–3.6,4.1 and8.1 govern approval/progression. The stakeholder track has two5EC courses and one7EC bachelor project, counted once although it spans two blocks. This current framework is not a guarantee of unchanged later-year delivery for a2026 entrant.
components: One permitted 15-EC minor from the approved EUR or authorised LDE offer; the choice needs to meet programme rules. Year 1 must be completed before entry.
A 5-EC elective within the 30-EC choice space. External units require Examination Board approval for level, supervision, limited overlap and fit with programme outcomes.
A second 5-EC elective within the same regulated choice space; elective status does not guarantee unrestricted choice or a place.
The final 5-EC elective in this minor-plus-electives pathway occurs in block 3.3 alongside Advanced Research Skills, as shown in the formal curriculum.
International Business and External Stakeholder Management
Selected track course. A full track must be taken; courses cannot be mixed across tracks. Allocation depends on preferences and capacity, so first choice is not guaranteed.
BSc Project Navigating Stakeholders in Global Business
A single 7-EC bachelor project belonging to the complete selected track; it spans blocks 3.4 and 3.5 and combines individual and group work. Year 1 must be complete before entry.

alternatives.label: International business & management
alternatives.concept: International business and management through strategy, marketing, organisations, leadership, finance and accounting, supported by economics, empirical research, data analysis and transnational law. Venture planning and product development provide specific complementary approaches to business strategy and innovation.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the broad business/management substance. Entrepreneurship is a specific complementary method, not a separately established bachelor specialisation.
progression: Business, economics and data study begin in Year 1; methods follow before advanced econometrics and organisational research. Practical finance follows the required business gateway. Accounting is studied later; the enriched finance description does not require prior accounting. Course availability and formal prerequisites are checked for every placement.
traceOverrides: examines managerial and organisational implications of AI and technological change within a broad international-business curriculum
introduces machine-learning models for evidence-based analysis within the programme's data and technology strand
develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions
Direct contribution: financial-data analysis, risk assessment, investment and budgeting implement the broad programme’s financial-decision strand.

alternatives.label: Business, AI & digital transformation
alternatives.concept: Business and digital transformation with a substantial technical AI strand. Strategy, organisations, international business, accounting, consumer behaviour and market research connect with programming, data science, machine learning, neural networks and AI ethics. Mathematics and algorithms provide specific technical foundations; this programme does not reproduce RSM’s full business-function curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum retains a substantial business core while adding a sequenced programming, mathematics, data, algorithms and AI strand, so the label names both business and AI.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces much of the general economics, law, communication and leadership mix with programming, mathematics, algorithms, databases, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics.
progression: Business, programming, data and mathematical foundations precede advanced algorithms, machine learning and neural networks. Research methods precede the final market-research course. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, mathematical statistics and neural networks; programming precedes algorithms.

candidates.label: Accounting and Finance for International Business

routeSelection.basis: The stakeholder track is retained because its broad international-business, internal/external stakeholder and workforce remit most directly continues the generic programme identity; AI and specialist accounting/finance tracks narrow that identity. The official track order also places it first. This choice is independent of UCR fit; complete-track and capacity rules apply.

selection.assessment: Two alternatives survive. The separate accounting/finance candidate cannot be sustained by the actual UCR offer: the two directly relevant7.5EC courses provide introductory accounting/statement analysis and practical financial decisions, not a substantial international accounting, capital strategies, multinational tax or advanced corporate-finance sequence. Its general economics/computing courses do not remedy that shortfall. A broad analytical-business relabelling would either retain that unsupported claim or duplicate the broad response. Responsible/sustainable business is concretely embedded in the broad programme’s product-development, AI governance, organisational and global-business content; it does not justify arbitrary substitutions to manufacture a third. The previously exported finance programme is removed.

blocks: Both develop a business plan; UCR develops a new venture, while RSM investigates an existing company.
Shared primary subject: developing and implementing business strategy. UCR adds a digital-transformation focus.
Shared subject: cultural diversity, inclusive leadership and managing a diverse workforce; this is a partial relationship.
Shared subject: motivation, groups, leadership, organisational culture and structure.
Shared subject: accounting information and analysis of financial statements.
Shared subject: financial decisions, risk, investments and budgeting; the respective scope and credit weights differ.
UCR includes consumer and firm behaviour, markets and incentives alongside macroeconomics.
Shared research design and quantitative/statistical analysis. RSM has a10EC business-oriented component; UCR is a general7.5EC methods course.
Regression-based quantitative analysis is an important part of the official Methods Master Classes. UCR uses Stata; RSM also covers other methods and R workflows.
Shared mathematical foundation, with different specific scope and credit weights.
Shared probability and mathematical statistics; UCR has a mathematical gateway prerequisite and greater allocated credit.
Shared primary subject: marketing strategy and consumer behaviour; UCR adds digital/AI marketing.
Shared subject: technology and managerial/organisational change; UCR focuses on AI and does not reproduce the TU Delft collaboration.
Shared business-law subject through transnational contracts, trade and legal risk.
The strongest direct subject counterpart is international business, including institutions, global trade, political/cultural forces and governance.

notes.text: RSM provides a compulsory sequence across business functions, a complete third-year track and a required bachelor project. The UCR options offer broad business and management, or business with technical AI. They leave gaps in operations, supply-chain management, human-resource management, management accounting and RSM’s particular track/project structure. Shared rows show specific partial subject or method relationships; they do not establish course equivalence.

audience.programmeDescription: International Business Administration at Rotterdam School of Management, Erasmus University Rotterdam is a three-year, English-taught BSc. Students study the major business functions in an international setting, develop quantitative research skills, use regulated choice space and complete one third-year track with a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options pursue broad international business and management, or business with a substantial technical AI strand. Both respond to the programme’s business questions through different course combinations. They do not reproduce its full compulsory functional sequence or multinational accounting/finance specialisms. Shared rows indicate particular subject or method relationships; blank cells preserve gaps.

curriculum.limitation: One permitted current track is shown; capacity and preference allocation apply, and track courses cannot be mixed. The 30-EC choice pathway shown contains an approved 15-EC minor and three 5-EC electives, with the last elective in block 3.3. Year 2/3 study requires positive binding study advice; the minor, electives, track and bachelor project require Year 1 completed. Approved exceptions and individual plans may apply. Later-year offers can change.
